title: Greece's transport ministry presents an AI system to transcribe stationmaster-driver GSM-R dialogues in real time and check them against protocols
summary: In a SKAI interview, Greece’s transport minister described AI transcription of GSM-R conversations and checks against railway communication protocols; no measured safety result was given.
account: In a SKAI interview reported on May 18, 2026, Deputy Minister of Transport Konstantinos Kyranakis described an AI system that transcribes GSM-R communications between stationmasters and train drivers. He said that it would identify departures from railway communication protocols so that the control center could intervene. He said that the system had been presented the previous Saturday. The interview supplies no developer, operational start date, transcription accuracy, alert counts, or measured safety result.
purpose: The system is intended to monitor operational radio communications and flag departures from protocol for the control center.
system: Speech-to-text and AI protocol-compliance monitoring of GSM-R stationmaster-driver communications (supplier not named)
deployer: Hellenic Ministry of Infrastructure and Transport (planned)
taxonomy_note: Announcement only; compliance checking of rail communications is read as a safety detection mechanism.

ai_role.statement: Kyranakis described speech transcription and checks against communication protocols. The original interview does not establish that the system was operating routinely or that an alert prevented an incident.
